report: Reassessed the complete canonical_cycles claim and its sole implementation/test association. The implementation entry in semantic_spec.rs is explicitly TODO: provisional inductive cutoff and depth limits do not provide path-kind-aware canonical-cycle fixpoints. The sole test sage_meta::todo::solver_canonical_cycles is an assertion-free TODO, not behavioral evidence. Its stated matrix covers repeated canonical goals with inductive failure, coinductive success and unknown-path ambiguity; converging and nonconverging provisional fixpoints; nonrepeating growth overflow; and ready-queue independence. Thus all claim aspects remain explicitly deferred, including deterministic structural bounds distinguishing infinitely growing distinct goals from ordinary repeated-goal lookup. Prerequisites are path-kind-aware cycle evaluation, provisional fixpoint handling, deterministic structural resource limits and a harness exercising recursive clause families under ready-queue perturbations. These are justified implementation and verification gaps, not claims of completion. For example treating distinct growing goals as cycles or letting polling order choose an outcome would violate the claim; the empty test currently detects neither, and the TODO matrix records that missing coverage. No additional edits are needed to the existing deferral accounting. Baseline verification: independently compared current whole-file bytes against both historical implementation_sources and test_sources; both exactly match. Current complete claim, metadata, TODO explanation and test body were independently inspected; historical approval was not substituted for this assessment. Captured review policy with review read; no additional behavioral helper was relied upon. Execution: ran review start, review read and byte comparisons; no behavioral tests or build were run by this reviewer. The coordinator reports 321 sage-meta tests and cargo build passed, separate execution evidence that does not prove this deferred claim.
